newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas prices rise on plant outages.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas prices rise on plant outages.

text.p: Canadian natgas prices extended their gains Tuesday as supplies remained tight in the Northwest due to plant outages, traders said.
Spot gas at the AECO storage hub in Alberta was quoted at C$1.64/1.65 per gigajoule, up an average of eight cents.
"We still haven't seen field receipts coming back. They're just not showing up as people expected. It's just one hiccup after another," a Calgary-based trader said.
July and July/October AECO were also talked firmer at C$1.61-1.63, while one-year gas in Alberta was quoted at C$1.77-1.78.
Storage injections slowed to about 800 million cubic feet on Monday, one trader said, adding that pace needed to continue to ensure ample inventories for the next heating season.
At Sumas, Wash., prices also rose three cents to about $1.42-1.47 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) as an outage in British Columbia continued to keep supplies scarce.
Westcoast Energy's 750 million cubic feet a day Fort Nelson gas plant in northeastern B.C., is expected to return to service later this week following a maintenance outage.
In eastern Canada, prices at Niagara eased by one cent to about $2.33-2.36 per mmBtu in pursuit of futures.
NYMEX's July Henry Hub gas futures rose 2.8 cents early to a high of $2.175, but at 1431 EDT the contract was down 0.7 cent at $2.14.
Temperatures in Toronto were still forecast to reach highs in the mid-70s over the next two days, according to Weather Services Corp.
